model_answer:
**Amazon (AMZN)** plans to spend by far the most.

Based on the most recent guidance (each company's Q3 2025 earnings reports, late October 2025):

| Company | 2025 Capex Plan | Trend |
|---|---|---|
| **Amazon (AMZN)** | **~$125 billion** (cash capex) | Up from ~$83B in 2024; management says it will rise again in 2026 |
| **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | **$91–93 billion** | Raised from ~$85B; "significant increase" expected in 2026 |
| **Meta (META)** | **$70–72 billion** (incl. finance lease principal) | Raised from $66–72B; 2026 growth to be "notably larger" |

Key details:
- **Amazon:** CFO Brian Olsavsky said on the Q3 call (Oct. 30, 2025): "we expect our full-year cash CapEx to be approximately $125 billion in 2025, and we expect that amount will increase in 2026." It had already spent $89.9B through Q3, with the bulk going to AWS AI infrastructure and custom silicon (Trainium). Note this excludes finance leases, so on a comparable basis its total would be even higher.
- **Alphabet:** Raised 2025 guidance to $91–93B (from ~$85B), with ~60% of spend on servers and 40% on data centers/networking. Q3 capex alone was $24B.
- **Meta:** Guided to $70–72B, up from $66–72B, driven by data centers and higher infrastructure hardware costs. Meta also said dollar growth in capex will be "notably larger" in 2026.

So Amazon is the biggest spender in 2025 by a wide margin — roughly $30B+ more than Alphabet and over $50B more than Meta (though Meta's pace of increase is steepening fastest into 2026).
